title: Model companies as first-class entities
body: Introduce a company schema so the owner’s company, clients, holding companies, spun-off legal entities, vendors, and other organizations have stable records. Distinguish display and legal identity, operational status, company type, domains, external identifiers, and notes. One record should represent one legal or operational entity; relationships between entities belong in a separate model. This is part of the broader organizational data model and must integrate with people, projects, engagements, and party references.

title: Track person-company affiliations over time
body: Introduce an affiliation schema connecting one canonical person to one company, with role, title, start and end dates, status, and notes. The same person may represent multiple companies simultaneously or historically, including a consultant, a holding company, and a spun-off legal entity. The affiliation should be usable from project participation and person aliases without duplicating the person identity.

title: Track typed person aliases and contact identities
body: Introduce separate alias records for email addresses, display names, usernames, phone numbers, legal names, and similar identity values. Each alias should identify its type, value, optional company affiliation, validity dates, primary/current status, and notes, so several organizational email addresses can resolve to one canonical person while preserving history and provenance.

title: Model project parties and representation context
body: Introduce project-party relationship records that connect projects to people, companies, or people acting through a specific company affiliation. Each relationship has a role, start and end dates, responsibility context, and notes. This replaces duplicated project stakeholder and person project lists and supports delivery parties, clients, sponsors, vendors, partners, and other participants.

title: Create flexible project role definitions
body: Introduce a reusable role catalog plus project-specific role definitions. A project can define roles appropriate to its type, scale, and complexity, including descriptions, required or optional status, expected quantity, and custom roles. Individual assignments should reference one role per project-party relationship and preserve dated responsibility.

title: Model client engagements separately from projects
body: Introduce a lightweight engagement schema for the broader commercial relationship, statement of work, or client assignment that may contain multiple projects. Engagements should connect companies, people, projects, dates, status, and optional contract or SOW references. Engagement-to-project links should support many-to-many relationships with dates and notes.

title: Introduce hierarchical WBS elements and stable codes
body: Introduce a WBS element schema that decomposes a project into workstreams, deliverables, and work packages. Elements form a hierarchy with one parent, stable dotted codes, immutable internal IDs, type, scope description, status, dates, and a responsible project party. Tasks and commitments can link to work-package elements without making the WBS replace execution records.

title: Preserve WBS baselines and structural change history
body: Add append-only WBS change records and explicit baseline approval metadata. Record additions, removals, moves, renames, scope changes, and responsibility changes while retaining the current WBS for normal use. Published dotted codes should not be silently reused or reassigned. The model should support auditability without requiring a complete immutable snapshot for every edit.

title: Generalize person and company counterparties
body: Update relevant records so people and companies can both act as counterparties or participants. This includes commitments, waiting-on records, interactions, and decisions where organizational involvement is meaningful, while retaining unresolved names and person-specific semantics where necessary. Use a consistent structured party-reference pattern rather than free text or duplicated person-only fields.

title: Expand organizational and WBS vocabulary
body: Update the glossary with conceptual and relational definitions for company, legal entity, affiliation, alias, project party, role, engagement, WBS, WBS element, workstream, deliverable, work package, baseline, and change record. Identify each term’s authoritative schema, distinctions from related terms, key relationships, and representative examples without turning the glossary into a field-level reference manual.
